new_content.title: Solving one-step linear equations
new_content.intro: An equation is a balance: both sides hold the same value. To solve for x, you undo whatever is being done to x. You will practice that on the simplest equations first.

sections.heading: The rule: do the same thing to both sides
sections.body: An equation stays true only if you treat both sides the same way. So every move you make, you make on the left AND on the right. The goal is to get x alone on one side.
sections.example: If x + 7 = 12, the 7 is added to x. To undo an addition, you subtract. So subtract 7 from both sides.

sections.heading: When x has something added, subtract it
sections.body: Rule: if the equation is x + a = b, subtract a from both sides. The left side collapses to x, and the right side becomes b - a. That value is your answer.
sections.example:
x + 7 = 12
Subtract 7 from both sides: x + 7 - 7 = 12 - 7
Left side: x + 0 = x
Right side: 12 - 7 = 5
So x = 5.
Check: 5 + 7 = 12. True.

sections.heading: When x has something subtracted, add it
sections.body: Rule: if the equation is x - a = b, add a to both sides. This undoes the subtraction, so x stands alone. Then check by putting your answer back into the original equation.
sections.example:
x - 3 = 8
Add 3 to both sides: x - 3 + 3 = 8 + 3
Left side: x - 0 = x
Right side: 8 + 3 = 11
So x = 11.
Check: 11 - 3 = 8. True.

steps: Look at what is done to x: 7 is added to x.
To undo an addition, subtract. Subtract 7 from both sides so the equation stays balanced.
Check by substituting: 5 + 7 = 12, which matches the original equation.

common_mistakes: Mistake: adding 7 to both sides of x + 7 = 12 and writing x = 19. This move gives x + 14 = 19, so x = 5, not x = 19. You must undo the addition by subtracting 7 from both sides.
Subtracting 7 from only one side, for example writing x = 12 - 7 on the left but leaving the right side at 12. That writes x = 5 while the equation is no longer balanced. Subtract 7 from both sides.
In x - 3 = 8, subtracting 3 again instead of adding. This gives x = 5, and 5 - 3 = 2, not 8. The subtraction is undone by addition, so add 3 to get x = 11.
Reading x + 7 = 12 as x = 7 + 12. The 7 is being added to x, so removing it means subtracting, not adding. That answer gives 19 + 7 = 26.
new_content.summary: An equation is a balance, so every move touches both sides. Undo addition by subtracting, and undo subtraction by adding. Then substitute your answer back to check it.

check_questions.prompt: To solve x + 4 = 11, which move should you make first?
check_questions.rationale: The 4 is added to x, so the move that undoes it is subtraction. Subtracting 4 from both sides leaves x alone on the left.

check_questions.prompt: Solve x + 6 = 15. Type the value of x.
check_questions.rationale: Subtract 6 from both sides: x = 15 - 6 = 9. Checking, 9 + 6 = 15.
The 3 is subtracted from x, so the move that undoes it is adding. Adding 3 to both sides gives x = 8 + 3 = 11.

check_questions.prompt: Solve x - 9 = 4. Type the value of x.
check_questions.rationale: Add 9 to both sides to undo the subtraction: x = 4 + 9 = 13. Checking, 13 - 9 = 4.
